text: Then the LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by another and is an adulteress — love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love their raisin cakes."

versions.text: Then the LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by another and is an adulteress — love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love the raisin cakes of their festivals."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads simply "lovers of cakes of raisins"; the phrase "of their festivals" is added content with no basis in the text. If clarification is desired, it belongs in a footnote rather than the verse itself.

text:
So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a lethek of barley.[^1]

[^1]: A homer was roughly 220 liters of grain; a lethek was about half a homer.

versions.text: So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a lethek of barley.
versions.explanation: The transliterated measures "homer" and "lethek" will be opaque to listeners; a brief footnote giving approximate volumes would aid comprehension without altering the read-aloud text.

text: And I said to her, "You are to stay with me for a long time. You must not be a prostitute, and you must not belong to any other man — and I will be yours."
For the Israelites will remain a long time without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, without ephod or household idols.
Afterward the Israelites will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king; in the last days they will come trembling to the LORD and to his goodness.
